title: Lesson Plan — Percentage and Its Applications (Class 10 NIOS Mathematics)
subject: Mathematics
objectives: Convert freely between fractions, decimals and percentages.
Compute x % of a quantity and express one quantity as a percentage of another.
Apply increase / decrease formulas, including the multiplicative effect of successive percentage changes.
Solve profit / loss problems given any two of CP, SP, gain%, loss%.
Apply discount on marked price and combine with markup to find effective profit.
Apply the simple-interest and compound-interest formulas (yearly and sub-annual).
materials: Mock 'shopping' price tags for the markup-and-discount activity
Cards with various fractions, decimals and percents for a 'three forms of one number' sort
Calculator (one per pair) for compound-interest exercises
Worksheet handout — Percentage and Its Applications

activities.description: Quick mental-math sprint. Write 50 %, 25 %, 10 %, 1 %, 0.1 % on the board and ask students to give 50 % of 80, 25 % of 80, 10 % of 80, etc. Then ask: '10 % up + 10 % down — does it cancel out?' Collect guesses; reveal the multiplicative answer in the Explain phase.
teacher_actions: Promise the formal answer in the Explain phase.
student_actions: Compute mentally; race to call out answers.
Predict the 10 %-up-then-down answer; record their guess.

activities.description: Pair card sort: each pair gets cards labelled with fractions (1/4, 3/5, 1/8, 5/4, 1/40), decimals (0.25, 0.6, 0.125, 1.25, 0.025) and percents (25 %, 60 %, 12.5 %, 125 %, 2.5 %). They sort into groups of three (the same number expressed three ways).
teacher_actions: Pick a pair to explain their groupings.
student_actions: Verify each triple by quick mental arithmetic.

activities.description: Direct instruction in five blocks: (i) percent definition, conversions, x % of A, A as % of B; (ii) percentage change, the (1 ± p/100) multiplier, successive-percentage formula, with the 10 %-up-down example; (iii) profit / loss — formulas and worked examples; (iv) discount on MP, combined with markup; (v) simple interest formula and compound interest formula (yearly and half-yearly), with one worked example each.
teacher_actions: Build a 'three forms of one number' table on the board.
Stress 'profit % on CP, discount % on MP' as the chapter's biggest mnemonic.
Walk through the formulas, with verification examples.
student_actions: Take notes; replicate every worked example.
Predict each answer before the teacher writes it.
Add the formulas to a 'rules box' for quick reference.

activities.description: Worked-problem station. Students do six worksheet questions: one conversion, one increase/decrease, one profit-%, one combined markup-and-discount, one SI, one CI (yearly).
teacher_actions: Circulate; offer the smallest hint that unblocks a stuck student.
Collect common slips for the Evaluate phase.
Pair fast finishers with peers who need support.
student_actions: Self-check against a posted answer key.
Verify each answer by re-applying the relevant formula.

activities.description: Exit-ticket quiz: 6 questions, one per outcome, drawn from the bank. Students complete in 8 minutes; the teacher projects answers and runs a 4-minute discussion of the two items most students missed.
teacher_actions: Distribute exit-ticket; remind it is individual.
Tally; address top two miss items.
student_actions: Self-mark and write a one-line reflection.

activities.description: Set homework: rest of the worksheet, plus one CREATE prompt — 'Compute the maturity amount on ₹15000 at 8 % p.a. for 2 years under (i) simple interest, (ii) yearly compound interest, (iii) half-yearly compound interest. Comment on the differences.' Preview the next chapter (Instalment Buying) by noting that real-world commerce typically combines interest with periodic payments.

homework: Complete the remaining problems on the Worksheet — Percentage and Its Applications handout.
Compare maturity amounts on ₹15000 at 8 % p.a. for 2 years under (i) SI, (ii) yearly CI, (iii) half-yearly CI; comment on the differences.
Find the equivalent single discount for two successive discounts of 12 % and 8 %; verify by computing both ways.
assessment_ideas: Use the 6-item exit ticket as a quick formative check.
Set a 12-question quiz drawn from the chapter bank for the next class as summative.
Mark the LONG_ANSWER on the half-yearly CI calculation using the auto-grade rubric.
Run a 5-minute peer-grading round on the CREATE homework using a two-criterion rubric (correct formula? maturity amounts properly compared?).
references: NIOS Secondary Mathematics, Module 2, Lesson 8: Percentage and Its Applications.
NCERT Class 8 Mathematics, Chapter 8: Comparing Quantities (for the prerequisite background).
